vocab.term: To take something into consideration/ account
vocab.meaning_en: to consider or remember something when judging a situation
vocab.example_en: No business will succeed if it fails to take the needs of customers into account/into consideration.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to enter a market with the connotation that entrance to the industry was difficult.
vocab.example_en: It is difficult to break into the market for designer sportswear because there is too much competition from leading brands like Nike.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to uphold one's promise; to do as one says
vocab.example_en: I lent him a lot of money, so I hope that he keeps his word and repays the loan.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to come to an agreement
vocab.example_en: The directors of the company have reached a consensus on the new business plan. Dịch đại ý To reach a consensus: đạt được thỏa thuận Nghĩa: 2 bên cùng đồng ý với một quyết định nào đó, đi tới 1 thỏa thuận Ví dụ: Các giám đ ốc của công ty đã đ ạt được th ỏa thuận về kế hoạch kinh doanh mới.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.term: To make the most of something
vocab.meaning_en: to make something appear as good as p ossible; to exploit something; to get as much out of something as is possible.
vocab.example_en: They designed the advertisements to make the most of the product's features.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: if a company goes out of business, it stops doing business permanently, especially because it has failed
vocab.example_en: If we sold food at those prices we’d soon go out of business.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to collect information about what people buy and why they choose it.
vocab.example_en: Advertising companies do a lot of market research before they design promotion campaigns.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to decrease, to reduce
vocab.example_en: The company made cutbacks at their stores in New York and many employees were dismissed.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: Seek to prevent disappointment by establishing in advance what can realistically be achieved or delivered by a project, undertaking, cour se of action, etc.
vocab.example_en: the company needs to manage the expectations of investors by presenting a realistic figure for next year’s estimated profits.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to assess a situation and figure out (or guess) the outcome
vocab.example_en: We cannot make a precise calculation of the price until we have all the costs.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: refers to making a payment to a supplier later than the terms of the arrangement under which goods or services were purchased from the supplier.
vocab.example_en: The company pays one month in arrears to all its suppliers and employees.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to buy something at a usually public sale of goods or property, where people make higher and higher bids (= offers of money) for each thing, until the thing is sold to the person who will pay most
vocab.example_en: Buying a property at an auction can be a nerve -wracking or exhilerating experience.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to waste money or supplies, or to waste opportunities by not u sing them to your advantage
vocab.example_en: James squandered all his savings in an unsuccessful business venture to sell ice cream in Alaska.
vocab.translation_vi: lãng phí cơ hội/ số tiết kiệm
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: refers to regular costs required to run a busin ess, such as rent, electricity, wages etc
vocab.example_en: An increase in rents in the shopping mall increased the overhead costs of all the shops which operated there.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: an act of taking over a company by buying its shares
vocab.example_en: Sony made a successful takeover of the broadcasting company CBS.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the action of joining two or more businesses into one
vocab.example_en: The directors of Kentucky Fried Chicken and Burger King are considering a merger of the two companies.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: having many tasks to perform
vocab.example_en: Many employees of the company take time off work because of illness and stress due to the heavy workload.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: something that somebody gives you [usually money] because they have hurt you or damaged something that you own
vocab.example_en: I received a large sum of money as compensation for the injury which I sustained at work.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the money that a government receives from taxes or whic h a company receives from its business
vocab.example_en: The tax revenues of the government have fallen as a result of the economic crisis.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: working in an office, not a factory
vocab.example_en: The insurance company is offering some white-collar jobs if you want to apply.
vocab.translation_vi: nhân viên văn phòng/ dân công sở
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: connected with people who do physical work in industry
vocab.example_en: He’s a blue-collar worker in a car factory.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to have a business which you own
vocab.example_en: I was tired of working for other people, so I decided to run my own business.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to earn money
vocab.example_en: I used to earn a living as a teacher, but now I sell used cars.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to make their company appear more attractive to people
vocab.example_en: In order to enhance their public image , some companies donate large sums of money to charities.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to expand a business, usually a new one
vocab.example_en: The company started one year ago with only one shop, but they have grown the business and now have ten shops.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to achieve an advantage over another company or organization, often by providing the same goods or services at a lower price
vocab.example_en: The high quality of VW cars, combined with their affordable price, has enabled the company to gain a competitiveedge over all its rivals in world markets.
vocab.translation_vi: có được lợi thế cạnh tranh
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to increase profits to the highest possible level
vocab.example_en: The company has hired a marketing consultant to recommend how to maximize profits next year.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to operate a business in a particular way
vocab.example_en: It is important to conduct a business with honesty in order to gain the confidence of customers.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to lose one’s job
vocab.example_en: The car factory has closed and 1000 employees have been made redundant.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: a system in which you and your employer pay money regularly into a fund, to use when you retire from work
vocab.example_en: One of the benefits of working for a big corporation is that such large companies usually provide a good pension scheme.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 1 Business and money\B+ái 1 Business and money\1.BUSINESS AND MONEY.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to send out a programme on television or radio that may be false or exagerrated in order to gain support for a political leader, a party etc
vocab.example_en: The media in North Korea broadcast propaganda every day about the dangers of war with South Korea and the USA.
vocab.translation_vi: tuyên truyền qua đài phát thanh/ truyền hình
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: a p iece of writing which deals with the most important news item of the day.
vocab.example_en: Newspapers in my country often have a leading article on some sensational crime that has been committed.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the policy of the newspaper, as decided by the person in charge of producing the newspaper
vocab.example_en: The editorial policy of a newspaper determines whether serious news items are reported in a responsible way.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: is a type of journalism that presents little or no legitimate well - researched news and instead uses eye -catching headlines to sell more newspapers.
vocab.example_en: Techniques used in yellow journalism may include exaggerations of news events, scandal-mongering or sensationalism
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to include an item in a news report
vocab.example_en: The media nowadays carries too many stories about celebrities and trivia and not enough serious news.
vocab.translation_vi: truyền tải/ chứa đựng câu chuyện nào đó
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the reporting of news and sport in newspapers, tv, or radio.
vocab.example_en: The US presidential election received global news coverage, so that the whole world became interested in the outcome.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to be an important item of news in the newspapers, on radio or TV.
vocab.example_en: It seems that every insignificant event in the lives of celebrities makes front page headlines.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: newly received information about an event that is currently taking place
vocab.example_en: One disadvantage of the printed media is that it is unable to carry the latest breaking news stories.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: having the latest information
vocab.example_en: Newspapers are unable to provide up to the minute news coverage of events as they happen.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: information that is no longer interesting or new, because it has already been reported
vocab.example_en: Newspapers have now become only a source of stale news , which is a major reason why they have become less popular.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the decline in the number of copies of a newspaper sold each day
vocab.example_en: As a result of their falling circulation , newspapers are losing advertising revenue.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: A form of brand or advertising campaign that involves a well known person using their fame to help promote a product or service
vocab.example_en: Celebrity endorsement by famous TV stars is commonly used by companies to encourage consumers to trust and buy their products.
vocab.translation_vi: sự tham gia của người nổi tiếng
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to pay money regularly in order to receive a copy of a magazine
vocab.example_en: Those with a strong interest in a pa rticular field sometimes prefer to subscribe to a magazine which has articles relating to that area.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the economic area relating to money or how money is managed
vocab.example_en: Newspapers have increasingly t urned to providing expert, detailed analysis of recent events, for example in their financial or business sections.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: advertising a product or service on the internet
vocab.example_en: The growing popularity of online advertising has resulted in a loss of revenue for the printed media in general.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.term: to slash the prices of products
vocab.meaning_en: to reduce the price dramatically
vocab.example_en: Supermarkets, for example, always carry huge in -store advertisements when they slash the prices of products.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: not completely trusting or certain about something
vocab.example_en: Consumers must always be wary of the claims made in advertisements, because such claims are often exagerrated or untrue.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to make products popular by advertising them
vocab.example_en: Most large enterprises contract spe cialist marketing companies to promote their products.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to buy things suddenly without any planning and without considering the effects they may have
vocab.example_en: Advertising motivates consumers to buy goods impulsively.
vocab.translation_vi: mua hàng một cách bốc đồng
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to be influenced to buy things as a result of advertising
vocab.example_en: If consumers were not easily swayed by advertisements, the advertising industry would not exist.
vocab.translation_vi: bị dao động bởi quảng cáo
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the action of collecting information about what people buy
vocab.example_en: In deciding how to promote their products or services, businesses should first conduct market research.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: a situation in which companies or shops continually reduce their prices in order to attract customers away from their competitors
vocab.example_en: Advertising plays a key role in price wars between supermarkets.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to introduce a new product
vocab.example_en: Companies have recognised that the services of the marketing industry are essential to launch a new product successfully.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: consumers whom businesses aim at when selling their products
vocab.example_en: Companies which sell soft drinks, like Coca Cola, aim mainly at a target audience of children and adolescents.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the action of bringing the name of a company to the attention of the public
vocab.example_en: Advertising, not the quality of the product, is responsible for creating brand awareness among consumers, as can be seen by the success of market leaders such as Nike or Coca Cola.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: the hours during which most people are watching TV
vocab.example_en: Although advertising on prime time television is expensive, it is guaranteed to reach a large audience.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: broadcast media which use electronic technology, such as the internet, television, radio, DVDs etc
vocab.example_en: In contast to pri nt media, the electronic media are growing in popularity, especially among the youth.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: to control something by means of rules
vocab.example_en: Governments must impose regulations on the advertising industry in order to protect consumers.
vocab.translation_vi: đặt quy định cho cái gì
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: advertising on the radio or television, between or during programmes.
vocab.example_en: Commercial advertising on television provides the revenue for most TV channels.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: a method of selling things or taking orders for sales by telephone
vocab.example_en: Telemarketing has become a growth industry, employing millions of people across the world.
vocab.source_pdf: ielts_materials\pdfs\Top Vocabulary\Bài 10 Media and advertising\10.MEDIA AND ADVERTISING.pdf

vocab.meaning_en: impossible to understand, unbelievable
vocab.example_en: It is beyond comprehension that some politicians deny the reality of global warming
vocab.translation_vi: quá tầm hiểu biết/ nhận thức, không thể hiểu/ tin được

vocab.meaning_en: the process of analyzing information in an objective way, in order to make a judgment about it
vocab.example_en: Critical thinking skills enable students to evaluate information.

vocab.meaning_en: to widen the limit of your desires, knowledge, or interests by reading widely
vocab.example_en: Schools should broaden the literary horizons of pupils by encouraging them to read in class and at home.
vocab.translation_vi: mở mang hiểu biết văn học

vocab.meaning_en: a particular way of describing something
vocab.example_en: In order to be a creative writer, a good turn of phrase is not as important as imagination.

vocab.meaning_en: to think that something means more than it really does
vocab.example_en: It is important not to read too much into election promises, but rather to evaluate the actions of governments.

vocab.meaning_en: the act of getting used to a changed or new situation
vocab.example_en: Those who migrate to cities have to undergo a painful period ofreadjustment in their search for a better life.

vocab.meaning_en: to continue reading
vocab.example_en: In the busy lives which many people lead today, we have become accustomed to glance quickly at news stories and we fail to read on and discover the facts behind the headlines.

vocab.meaning_en: to do something in a different way
vocab.example_en: I believe that universities should break with precedent and admit more women to engineering and science courses.

vocab.meaning_en: to read something carefully from beginning to end to look for mistakes or check details
vocab.example_en: Attention to detail is so important in many jobs, so the practice of reading over one’s written work should be taught at school and university.
vocab.translation_vi: đọc kỹ, đọc từ đầu đến cuối

vocab.meaning_en: to become known by somebody
vocab.example_en: If it comes to the knowledge of your manager that you are honest and hard-working, your promotion prospects will be improved.

vocab.meaning_en: confident because you know that something is true or will happen
vocab.example_en: I would recommend that people should eat only organic food , safe in the knowledge that it contains no harmful chemicals.
vocab.translation_vi: chắc chắn về cái gì đó

vocab.meaning_en: to search thoroughly for information
vocab.example_en: Computer technology has enabled authorities to dig deep into all kinds of personal records relating to ordinary citizens.
vocab.translation_vi: đào sâu tìm hiểu về cái gì

vocab.term: to do something to the letter
vocab.meaning_en: to do exactly what somebody or something instructs, paying attention to every detail
vocab.example_en: It is important to apply the law to the letter, so that every illegal action is punished.

vocab.meaning_en: (of a memory, an image, etc.) to be remembered for a long time
vocab.example_en: When children learn a foreign language in primary school, words and phrases tend to stick in their minds almost without the effort of learning them in a formal way.

vocab.meaning_en: to become or make something better, more skilful, more effective, etc. than before
vocab.example_en: The opportunity to do an internship with a company enables students to sharpen up the theoretical knowledge gained at college.
vocab.translation_vi: làm cái gì đó thêm sâu sắc, nhạy bén

vocab.meaning_en: to decide that somebody or something is a failure and not worth paying attention to
vocab.example_en: Space projects should not be written off as expensive failures, because space represents the new frontier for exploration.
vocab.translation_vi: xóa bỏ/ loại bỏ cái gì

vocab.meaning_en: to be completely focused on something
vocab.example_en: A good work -life balance is important, because if people are too engrossed in their work their family life may suffer.

vocab.term: to understand somebody/something to be/have something
vocab.meaning_en: to think or believe that something is true because you have been told that it is
vocab.example_en: The President is understood to be in favour of more spending on the military.
vocab.translation_vi: tin cái gì đó/ cho là

vocab.meaning_en: to lead or guide somebody through or around something
vocab.example_en: Work experience conducts people who are new in a profession through some of the practical difficulties which they will face.
vocab.translation_vi: dẫn dắt, hướng dẫn ai đó

vocab.meaning_en: not worried because you are sure that nothing bad will happen
vocab.example_en: Students who work hard throughout the year will be confident when they take exams, secure in the knowledge that they are well - prepared.

vocab.meaning_en: stories told to children before they sleep
vocab.example_en: Parents should spend time with their children, for exa mple by telling them bedtime stories every night.
vocab.translation_vi: truyện kể trước khi đi ngủ

vocab.meaning_en: to be a history of particular events
vocab.example_en: The problem of waste disposal in my country has been a story of confusion and bad management.

vocab.meaning_en: to print an article, to show a news report
vocab.example_en: The media nowadays runs many stories on environmental concerns.

vocab.example_en: A lack of government programs for vaccination and regular health care may lead to the outbreak of an epid emic, particularly in developing countries.
vocab.translation_vi: sự bùng phát của dịch bệnh

vocab.meaning_en: involving little exercise or physical activity
vocab.example_en: A sedentary lifestyle is a major factor in health problems such as obesity and heart disease.
vocab.translation_vi: phong cách sống thiếu vận động

vocab.meaning_en: eating healthy food at regular times of the day
vocab.example_en: Health education involves teaching people about healthy eating habits, such as regular mealtimes and eating fruit and vegetables every day.
vocab.translation_vi: thói quen ăn uống lành mạnh

vocab.meaning_en: to do some physical activity on a regular basis
vocab.example_en: Authorities should encourage people of all ages to take regular exercise by providing facilities in each community.

vocab.meaning_en: a method or routine of taking regular exercise
vocab.example_en: Even elderly people can adopt a fitness regime by taking light exercise such as walking or jogging.

vocab.meaning_en: publicity to encourage people to be concerned about looking after their health.
vocab.example_en: Public health awareness campaigns are essential if people are to accept that they have a personal responsibility to look after their own health.
vocab.translation_vi: chiến dịch tuyên truyền sức khỏe

vocab.meaning_en: practices of healthcare intended to try to stop illnesses
vocab.example_en: An emphasis on preventive medicine will result in a healthier population and reduced costs for medical treatment.

vocab.meaning_en: this is a term used by many wes tern countries to describe more traditional types of healthcare that do not involve operations and pharmaceutical drugs.
vocab.example_en: Naturopathy is a form of alternative healthcare which treats illness and diseases using natural foods, herbs and other techniques.

vocab.meaning_en: the agencies funded by the government to protect and promote the health of the population
vocab.example_en: I would argue that funding for public health services should be the main priority of all governments.
vocab.translation_vi: Dịch vụ y tế công cộng

vocab.term: to take out private health insurance
vocab.meaning_en: to make regular payments to an insurance company, who will pay for medical or hospital treatment when you need it
vocab.example_en: In countries with poor public health services , many people have to take out private health insurance in order to receive adequate medical treatment.
vocab.translation_vi: đăng ký bảo hiểm y tế tư nhân

vocab.meaning_en: the medical treatment th at you receive first when you are sick or ill, for example from your doctor or local clinic.
vocab.example_en: Developing countries must allocate resources to establish primary health care clinics in rural areas and overcrowded city districts.
vocab.translation_vi: chăm sóc sức khỏe cơ bản

vocab.meaning_en: a person who works as a doctor or surgeon
vocab.example_en: It is essential to train more medical practitioners if public health is to be improved.

vocab.term: to build up one’s immune system/ immunity
vocab.meaning_en: to increase the ability of your body to fight diseases
vocab.example_en: A healthy lifestyle and a diet rich in vitamins is a sure way to build up one’s immune system.

vocab.meaning_en: related to illnesses of one’s mind
vocab.example_en: Overwork may sometimes re sult in mental health problems , such as anxiety and depression.

vocab.meaning_en: to give counselling to a person who is suffering from a mental health problem
vocab.example_en: Some schools in Europe now offer emotional support to pupils who are the victims of bullying.
vocab.translation_vi: đưa ra hỗ trợ tinh thần

vocab.meaning_en: to be unable to stop taking harmful drugs, tobacco or alcohol.
vocab.example_en: More specialist clinics, offering treatment and advice, are required to help people who are addicted to drugs.

vocab.meaning_en: the process of looking for a way to make a sick person hea lthy again
vocab.example_en: It is the responsibility of governments to enable doctors to search for a cure for diseases by providing adequate funding.

vocab.meaning_en: illnesses which are likely to kill somebody
vocab.example_en: Great advances have been made in the treatment of life- threatening conditions such as cancer and heart disease.

vocab.meaning_en: to have effects which could be bad for one’s health
vocab.example_en: Smoking and drinking alchohol are potentially dangerous habits, because they carry serious health risks.
vocab.translation_vi: mang hiểm họa tới sức khỏe

vocab.meaning_en: the money paid by a pati ent to receive medicines authorised by a doctor.
vocab.example_en: In Britain, the government has abolished prescription charges for elderly people, so that they no longer pay for the medicines they need.

vocab.meaning_en: a room in a hospital where doctors carry out surgery on patients
vocab.example_en: Safe hygiene standards are important throughout any hospital, but particularly in an operating theatre.

vocab.meaning_en: an industry which makes drugs and medicines
vocab.example_en: I believe that the pharmaceutical industry must be strictly regulated by governments, especially in the testing of new drugs.

vocab.meaning_en: an illness that becomes worse as time passes
vocab.example_en: Breakthroughs in medical science are providing more effective treatment for degenerative illnesses such as Alzheimer’s disease.
vocab.translation_vi: bệnh suy biến Nghĩa; căn bệnh có chuyển biến xấu hơn theo thời gian Ví d ụ: Đ ột phá trong ngành khoa h ọc dư ợc ph ẩm là cung c ấp nhi ều phương pháp đi ều tr ị hiệu qu ả cho căn b ệnh suy bi ến, ví d ụ như Alzheimer.

vocab.meaning_en: to be harmful to health
vocab.example_en: Lying in the sun for too long can be detrimental to health and result in skin cancers.

vocab.meaning_en: to have a regular examination carried out by a doctor or dentist
vocab.example_en: In order to identify health problems at an early stage, people should have a regular check-up so that preventive measures can be taken if necessary.
